The context

A shrinking market, an offer that all looks the same

Wine consumption is declining. Consumers no longer want just a bottle — they want meaning, transparency, a story. And for you, the challenge cuts both ways: every reference in your range needs to stand out to a customer facing ten identical-looking labels on the shelf.

↓

Wine consumption is declining steadily, and competition increasingly plays out on price alone — a game no one wins long-term.

?

The offer is hard to read for the end consumer: too much choice, not enough cues to tell one wine apart from another.

+

Customers want connection with the producer — the origin, the gesture, the authenticity — far more than a technical sheet.

How it works

Four simple steps. No app to download.

The concept is designed to be understood at a glance — by you and by your customers alike.

Step 1

You choose

240 references across every style and region — 51 with video today, 90+ coming soon. No minimum order.

Step 2

They scan

A discreet QR code built into the front label. In the shop, at the table, or back home — one scan, no app required.

Step 3

They watch

The winemaker's own video plays instantly, subtitled in their language — 15 available today. A few examples below.

Frissons des Anges Rosé — AOP Côtes de Provence
Domaine de l'Olivette Red — AOP Bandol
Gewurztraminer Grand Cru Steinert
Step 4

They come back

Next time, they may not ask for the same bottle — but they'll look for that same little label. Once a customer connects it with a wine worth remembering, it becomes a mark they trust and come back to, on any bottle that carries it.

Loyalty to the label Repeat-purchase driver Not one bottle — the mark
